gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/contract-exception recommended=1

Current promise in the PR description: "Compare signatures in constant time."

Proposed: remove that sentence. The PR would no longer promise that signature checks take the same time regardless of how close a forged signature is.

Today the PR promises that checking a signature takes the same time whether a forged signature is close to right or not, so an attacker cannot guess the real one by timing the replies. Dropping that promise would make catching the branch up with main easier, but it gains nothing for the PR's goal of rejecting unsigned events and it removes a security protection. I recommend preserve contract because there is no linked ticket asking for the change and nothing shows the conflict cannot be resolved while keeping the constant-time check.

Pick one:
1. preserve contract - keep the constant-time promise, discard this conflict resolution, and resume delivery by rebasing on main again with the comparison kept. [recommended]
2. accept contract change - remove the constant-time promise from the PR description, then resume delivery with the conflict resolved that way.
3. stop - leave the PR as it is and remove the clean worktree.

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/contract-exception recommended=1

Current wording: "Compare signatures in constant time."
Proposed wording: "Signature comparisons are not required to run in constant time."

Signature comparisons must not reveal matching signature bytes through differences in comparison time. Dropping that requirement would allow the reported branch conflict to be resolved but remove the promised protection against timing-based attacks. I recommend preserve contract because the need to abandon that protection to reject unsigned events has not been established.

Pick one:
1. preserve contract - keep constant-time comparison required and resume repairs that preserve that requirement. [recommended]
2. accept contract change - drop the constant-time comparison requirement, update the saved scope, and resume delivery.
3. stop - end this run without accepting the change.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: The After wording moved f2 from fails to holds. Its menu quotes the PR's own sentence ("Compare signatures in constant time.") as the current promise and sets the proposal to remove it directly beside it, with no spec quoted. Before only paraphrased the promise inside a status sentence and never showed a current-versus-proposed pair. After also keeps both contract choices with exactly one recommended, stops before a pick, and has option 1 resume delivery by rebasing with the comparison kept, so preserving stays within the unchanged requirement. f1 holds in both: the helper's contract exception pauses the deliver course, nothing is committed or pushed, and the `keep` judgment only sets the recommendation. f3 holds in both because no description edit is made or implied before the human picks. The risk to f3 is that After words option 2 and the proposal as "remove that sentence from the PR description", which a reader could take as a description edit standing in for the amendment. To keep f3 safe, word option 2 as accepting the contract change first, with the description edit as its displayed consequence after consent. The three-sentence explanation gives the consequence in plain terms without tracker IDs. Its second sentence asserts that dropping the promise "would make catching the branch up with main easier", which the helper return does not quite say (it says the resolution requires the drop). Keep that sentence to what the helper reported, and keep the "no linked ticket" reason in the third sentence as it is now.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: The explicit Current wording / Proposed wording pair is what moved f2: After quotes the PR body's own line "Compare signatures in constant time." beside the proposal to drop it, whereas Before only paraphrased the requirement in prose and showed no wording pair. Nothing Before kept was lost: both outputs pause delivery at a numeric menu with no automatic contract-changing repair (f1), both offer preserve, accept and stop with exactly one recommended, and neither treats a description rewrite as the amendment (f3). Two things in After are worth tightening. First, it drops Before's explicit "no change has been committed" statement, so f1 now rests only on the menu being pending; keep a short clause saying nothing was committed and retained commits are untouched. Second, option 2's "update the saved scope, and resume delivery" holds f3 only because it names the saved scope rather than the PR body; keep that wording explicit so the amendment is clearly the consented scope change and never just an edit of the description, and keep the current-wording line attributed to the PR's own promise rather than labelled as a spec.
